Assign to a constant named `css` a string that contains **one CSS style rule** for `h1` elements that sets:

- the font size to `40px`

The checker adds your rule to the page's style sheet.

setup.css: body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }

hints: A rule is a selector followed by declarations in braces: h1 { property: value; }

tests.name: css is a string with one rule

questions.title: HTML5 semantic page layout
questions.prompt:
Assign to a constant named `html` a string of HTML for a page body that uses the HTML5 **semantic elements**, in this order:

1. a `header` that contains an `h1`
2. a `main` that contains a `section` with an `h2` and a `p`
3. a `footer` that contains a `p`

Any text is fine. (Template literals let a string span several lines.)
hints: Use backticks for a multi-line string.
The semantic elements are header, nav, main, section, article, aside and footer.

tests.name: html is a string
tests.code: return typeof html === "string";

tests.name: Has header > h1, main > section > h2 + p, footer > p
Elements are in the order header, main, footer

questions.title: div versus span
questions.prompt:
Assign to `html` a string with a `div` that has the id `notice`. Inside it, put a paragraph with the text `Sale ends Friday`, where only the word **Friday** is wrapped in a `span` with the class `highlight`.

`div` is a block element for grouping; `span` is an inline element for marking part of a line.

tests.name: div#notice contains a p
tests.code:
const d = new DOMParser().parseFromString(html, "text/html");
return !!d.querySelector("div#notice > p");

tests.name: Paragraph text is "Sale ends Friday"
tests.code:
const d = new DOMParser().parseFromString(html, "text/html");
return d.querySelector("#notice p").textContent.trim() === "Sale ends Friday";

tests.name: Only "Friday" is in span.highlight

questions.title: Static versus dynamic pages
questions.prompt:
For each task, decide where it is processed in a web application: by the **web server** (`"server"`) or in the **browser** (`"client"`). Assign an object named `where` with these properties, each set to `"server"` or `"client"`:

- `runPhp` — running PHP code to build a page from a database
- `runJavaScript` — running the JavaScript in a `<script>` element
- `applyCss` — applying CSS to render the page
- `querySql` — querying a database with SQL
- `validateFormBeforeSubmit` — checking a form's fields before it is sent
hints: The browser handles HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Server-side languages and the database run on the server.

tests.name: where is an object with 5 answers
tests.code: return typeof where === "object" && Object.keys(where).length === 5;

tests.name: Server-side tasks are correct
tests.code: return where.runPhp === "server" && where.querySql === "server";

tests.name: Client-side tasks are correct
tests.code: return where.runJavaScript === "client" && where.applyCss === "client" && where.validateFormBeforeSubmit === "client";
